naming: Names are the names of the framework; `words` are their words in lower case, for each backend to apply the casing of its language.

functions.name: ferro_abi_version
functions.doc: The version of the ABI ([`FERRO_ABI_VERSION`]). A binding checks it before its first call. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_show
functions.doc: Shows the window `window` ([`ferro_create`](crate::ferro_create) of the type `Window`). While it is open the library holds it (its handle can be released), and the main loop of [`ferro_app_run`] runs until the last window shown this way closes. [`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] before `ferro_app_run` has started. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_close
functions.doc: Closes the window `window`, as its close button does. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_quit
functions.doc: Ends the main loop of [`ferro_app_run`] once the work at hand is done; the open windows are left as they are. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_app_run
functions.doc: Runs an application on the platform of the operating system (macOS, Windows or Linux, with the Fluent theme): makes the calling thread the UI thread ([`ferro_init`](crate::ferro_init); on macOS it must be the main thread), sets the application up, calls `on_start(token)`, and runs the main loop until the last window shown with [`ferro_show`] closes or [`ferro_quit`] is called; then returns [`FERRO_OK`](crate::FERRO_OK). `on_start` creates the windows and shows them; if it returns a value other than `0` the loop does not run and the result is [`FERRO_START_FAILED`](crate::FERRO_START_FAILED). `options` is reserved and must be `NULL` in ABI version 1. Runs once per process ([`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] the second time). With the environment variable `FERROUI_SMOKE_EXIT_MS=<n>` the windows close after `n` milliseconds, as for every sample of the repository (the smoke runs of continuous integration). A build without the desktop platform (the feature `desktop` of `ferroui-capi`) returns [`FERRO_NOT_SUPPORTED`](crate::FERRO_NOT_SUPPORTED).

functions.name: ferro_last_error
functions.doc: The message of the last call that failed on the calling thread, as UTF-8 with a NUL at the end; an empty string when none has failed. Successful calls leave it as it is (as `errno`). The text stays valid until the next failure on the thread. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_last_error_code
functions.doc: The status code of the last call that failed on the calling thread ([`FERRO_OK`] when none has failed): the code of a function that returns a handle, which is `0` on a failure. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_clear_error
functions.doc: Forgets the last failure of the calling thread: [`ferro_last_error_code`] is [`FERRO_OK`] and [`ferro_last_error`] empty until the next failure. A binding whose language reports errors as values (Osprey's `Result`) clears it before a call whose result does not tell a failure apart (a getter with a fallback) and reads the code after it. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_event_x
functions.doc: The horizontal position of the pointer of the routed event being handled (a pointer event, or a tap: `Tapped`, `DoubleTapped`), relative to the visual `relative_to`, or to the top level the event happened in for `0`. NaN on a failure (recorded: [`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] outside a handler, [`FERRO_NOT_SUPPORTED`] for an event without a position). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_event_y
functions.doc: The vertical position of the pointer of the routed event being handled; see [`ferro_event_x`]. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_event_button
functions.doc: The button a pointer event being handled is about: `1` left, `2` right, `3` middle, `4` and `5` the first and second extra buttons (the values of `MouseButton`), for a press or a release; `0` for a pointer event that is not about a button (a move). A negative status for an event that is not a pointer event, or outside a handler. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_event_key
functions.doc: The key of the key event being handled (`KeyDown`, `KeyUp`), as the name of the member of `Key` (`Return`, which is also named `Enter`; `Escape`; `A`), NUL-terminated and owned by the library until the next call of `ferro_event_key` on the thread. `NULL` on a failure (recorded: an event that is not a key event, or outside a handler). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_focus
functions.doc: Moves the keyboard focus to `object` (an input element: a text box, a button), as a click on it does. [`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] when it cannot take the focus now (it is not focusable, not enabled, or not in a shown window yet: posting the call with [`ferro_post`](crate::ferro_post) focuses it once it is). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_subscribe
functions.doc: Attaches `function` to the event `event` ([`ferro_event_id`](crate::ferro_event_id)) of `object`: it is called with `token` on every raise of the event, on the UI thread (see [`FerroEventFn`]). For a routed event the handler listens to the direct and the bubbling route of events that are not handled yet, and a result other than `0` marks the event as handled. Returns a positive subscription ID for [`ferro_unsubscribe`], or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_subscribe_dispatch
functions.doc: [`ferro_subscribe`] to the one dispatcher of the thread ([`ferro_frame_dispatcher`](crate::ferro_frame_dispatcher)): every raise of the event calls it with `tag`, the sender and the argument, as an event bound in a frame does (the event text and number are empty). For a binding with one dispatcher, which then needs no trampoline of its own between the library and its dispatcher: one indirect call per event. Returns a positive subscription ID for [`ferro_unsubscribe`], or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_subscribe_data
functions.doc: [`ferro_subscribe`] with a `void *` in place of the token: `function` is called with `user_data`, and `release` (which may be `NULL`) is called with it once the handler is gone, removed by [`ferro_unsubscribe`] or dropped with its object. If the subscription fails, `release` is called before this returns. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_unsubscribe
functions.doc: Removes the handler of the subscription `subscription` ([`ferro_subscribe`]); its user data is released ([`ferro_subscribe_data`]). [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] for an ID that is not a live subscription. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_raise
functions.doc: Raises the routed event `event` on `object` with plain event arguments, as the control does when it raises it (`Click` of a button, as a click does): for tests and for driving an interface from code. [`FERRO_NOT_SUPPORTED`] for an event whose arguments carry more than the routing state (a pointer event). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_result
functions.doc: Gives the size of the measure or arrange callback that runs now (the innermost), for a language that cannot write through the `double *` of the callback. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_register
functions.doc: Registers the class `name` (UTF-8, `length` bytes, negative for NUL-terminated) on the base `base` (`FERRO_BASE_CONTROL`, `_PANEL`, `_DECORATOR`, `_CONTENT_CONTROL`) and returns its type ID, or a negative status. The class is created by name ([`ferro_create`](crate::ferro_create) with [`ferro_type_id`](crate::ferro_type_id)), in frames and wherever a class is found by name; its virtual members call the callbacks set with `ferro_class_on_*`, and fall through to the base where none is set. At most 64 classes per process. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_create
functions.doc: Sets the callback that gives each new instance of the class its data (`NULL` for none). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_measure
functions.doc: Sets the measure callback of the class (`NULL`: the base measures). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_arrange
functions.doc: Sets the arrange callback of the class (`NULL`: the base arranges). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_render
functions.doc: Sets the render callback of the class (`NULL`: the base renders alone). The base renders first (the background of a panel); the callback draws over it. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_property_changed
functions.doc: Sets the callback called when a property the class registered changes, with its ID. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_attached
functions.doc: Sets the callback called when an instance is attached to the visual tree. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_detached
functions.doc: Sets the callback called when an instance is detached from the visual tree. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_apply_template
functions.doc: Sets the callback called when the template of an instance is applied (a class on `FERRO_BASE_CONTENT_CONTROL`); [`ferro_template_part`] finds its parts. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_pointer
functions.doc: Sets the callback of pointer presses, releases and moves on an instance. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_on_key
functions.doc: Sets the callback of key presses and releases on an instance. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_class_set_data
functions.doc: Sets the data of the class, given to its create callback. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_object_set_data
functions.doc: Sets the data of an instance of a foreign class, passed to every callback of the instance, and the function that releases it when the instance goes away (`NULL` for none). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_object_data
functions.doc: The data of an instance of a foreign class (`NULL` for none or on a failure, recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_property_register
functions.doc: Registers a property of the foreign class `owner` (a type ID of [`ferro_class_register`]) and returns its property ID, or a negative status. `kind` is a kind of signal (`FERRO_SIGNAL_I64`, `_F64`, `_BOOL`, `_TEXT`); the default is `default_number` (an integer or a boolean as a number) or `default_text` (UTF-8, NUL-terminated, `NULL` for no text). `flags` combine `FERRO_PROPERTY_AFFECTS_MEASURE`, `_ARRANGE`, `_RENDER`, `_INHERITS` and `_ATTACHED` (an attached property, `Owner.Name`, that every control takes). The property is a styled property as the ones of the framework: the setters and getters of the ABI, frames, signals, styles, bindings and animations use it. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_measure
functions.doc: Measures `object` (a child, from a measure callback) at the available size. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_arrange
functions.doc: Arranges `object` (a child, from an arrange callback) in the rectangle. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_desired_width
functions.doc: The desired width of `object` after its measure (`0` on a failure, recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_desired_height
functions.doc: The desired height of `object` after its measure (`0` on a failure, recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_bounds_width
functions.doc: The width `object` was arranged at (its bounds; `0` on a failure, recorded): what a render callback of a language without instance data draws in. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_layout_bounds_height
functions.doc: The height `object` was arranged at (its bounds; `0` on a failure, recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_panel_child_count
functions.doc: The number of children of a panel (`0` for another object, recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_panel_child
functions.doc: The child `index` of a panel, with one reference counted (release it), or `0` (recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_template_part
functions.doc: The part named `name` of the applied template of `object` (a foreign class on `FERRO_BASE_CONTENT_CONTROL`), with one reference counted (release it), or `0` with [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`]. From the apply-template callback on. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_draw_brush
functions.doc: A solid brush of the colour `argb` (`0xAARRGGBB`) for the `ferro_draw_*` functions: its ID (a positive number), the same for the same colour, or a negative status. Make the brushes of a control once (at its creation) and draw with their IDs. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_draw_pen
functions.doc: A solid pen of the colour `argb` and the thickness `thickness`: its ID, or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_draw_rect
functions.doc: Fills (`brush`) and strokes (`pen`) a rectangle, its corners rounded by `radius_x` and `radius_y`. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_ellipse
functions.doc: Fills and strokes the ellipse in the rectangle. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_line
functions.doc: Strokes a line with the pen. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_path
functions.doc: Fills and strokes the geometry of the path data `data` (the mini-language of markup: `M 0,0 L 10,10 Z`, UTF-8, `length` bytes, negative for NUL-terminated). UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_text
functions.doc: Draws `text` (UTF-8, `length` bytes, negative for NUL-terminated) with its top left at `x`, `y`, in the default typeface at `size`, with the brush. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_push_clip
functions.doc: Clips what is drawn next to the rectangle, until [`ferro_draw_pop`]. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_push_transform
functions.doc: Transforms what is drawn next by the matrix (`m11 m12 m21 m22 dx dy`), until [`ferro_draw_pop`]. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_push_opacity
functions.doc: Draws what is drawn next with the opacity, until [`ferro_draw_pop`]. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_draw_pop
functions.doc: Pops the clip, transform or opacity pushed last in the context. UI thread only, in a render callback.

functions.name: ferro_frame_begin
functions.doc: Starts a frame on the calling thread: empties the buffer of the scalar writer. Any thread (the buffer is the calling thread's); commit it on the UI thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_open
functions.doc: Opens an element of the class `type_id` ([`ferro_type_id`](crate::ferro_type_id)) in the frame of the calling thread. `key` tells siblings apart across frames: `0` keeps the element by its position among the siblings without a key. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_key_str
functions.doc: Gives the element opened last a text key in place of its integer key. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_close
functions.doc: Closes the element opened last in the frame of the calling thread. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_str
functions.doc: Sets `property` of the open element from text, as [`ferro_set_str`] does when the frame is committed. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_str16
functions.doc: Sets `property` of the open element from UTF-16 text (`units` code units), for a language whose strings are UTF-16. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_f64
functions.doc: Sets `property` of the open element from a number, as [`ferro_set_f64`] does. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_i64
functions.doc: Sets `property` of the open element from an integer or the value of an enumeration member, as [`ferro_set_i64`] does. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_bool
functions.doc: Sets `property` of the open element from a boolean, as [`ferro_set_bool`] does. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_on
functions.doc: Binds the event `event` ([`ferro_event_id`](crate::ferro_event_id)) of the open element to the message tag `tag`: when it fires, the dispatcher of the thread ([`ferro_frame_dispatcher`]) is called with the tag, the sender, and the value of `value_property` (`0` for none), whose text and number [`ferro_frame_event_text`] and [`ferro_frame_event_f64`] give. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_bind
functions.doc: Binds `property` of the open element to the signal slot `slot` (docs/c-abi.md, section 14): the commit binds it ([`ferro_signal_bind`](crate::ferro_signal_bind)) and keeps the binding while the frames keep the record, so a write of the slot updates the property with no new frame. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_memo
functions.doc: Makes the open element a memo element: its subtree is what `version` says it is (a revision of the data it shows, a hash of it), and the tags of its events are `tag_base` plus offsets that the version fixes. While the element keeps its key and its version, a commit does not look into its subtree (a new `tag_base` moves its tags), and with an integer key the next frame can reuse it whole ([`ferro_frame_reuse`]). A different subtree under the same key and version is the caller's error: the commit keeps the old one. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_frame_reuse
functions.doc: Writes the memo element with the integer key `key` and the version `version` of the last frame committed under `root` ([`ferro_frame_memo`]) into the frame of the calling thread as one record, in place of its whole subtree, with its tags moved to start at `tag_base`. Returns the number of tags the subtree uses (`0` or more: the next tag of the caller is `tag_base` plus it), or a negative status, and then writes nothing: [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] when the root has no such element (nothing is recorded; the caller writes the element in full), or [`FERRO_WRONG_THREAD`](crate::FERRO_WRONG_THREAD) off the UI thread. Commit the frame under the same root, before another commit under it. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_commit
functions.doc: Commits the frame of the scalar writer of the calling thread under `root` (see [`ferro_frame_commit_bytes`]) and empties the buffer. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_commit_bytes
functions.doc: Commits the frame of `length` bytes at `data` (records of the layout of the API model) under `root`: the elements at the top of the frame become the children of `root` (the content of a window, the children of a panel), and the frame before it under the same root is reconciled into this one. With a `root` of `0` the elements at the top are windows: shown ([`ferro_show`](crate::ferro_show)) when they come and closed when they go, which needs the application to run ([`ferro_app_run`](crate::ferro_app_run)). The library keeps a reference to `root` until [`ferro_frame_clear`]. A failed write does not stop the commit: the first failure is returned and recorded. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_dispatcher
functions.doc: Sets the dispatcher of the events bound in frames, one for the process: called on the UI thread with the tag of the binding, the sender (borrowed for the call) and the value of its value property as an integer (a number truncated, a boolean as `0` or `1`). A result other than `0` marks a routed event as handled. `NULL` stops dispatching. Any thread: a language whose callbacks must be named functions at the call site (Osprey) sets it before [`ferro_app_run`](crate::ferro_app_run).

functions.name: ferro_frame_dispatch
functions.doc: Calls the dispatcher of the thread ([`ferro_frame_dispatcher`]) with `tag`, `sender` and `arg` as an event would, and returns its result: a binding starts its loop with it (the tag `0` asks for the first frame), its one trampoline forwards the events of its subscriptions with it, and a test drives a message without an event. The event text and number are empty. [`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] (as a negative result) without a dispatcher. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_event_text
functions.doc: The text of the value property of the event being dispatched, NUL-terminated and owned by the library until the next event; empty for a binding without a value property or outside a dispatch. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_event_f64
functions.doc: The value property of the event being dispatched as a number (`0` when it is not one). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_find
functions.doc: The handle of the element with the integer key `key` in the retained tree of `root`, with one reference counted (release it), or `0` with [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`]: for tests and for driving an interface built from frames. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_frame_clear
functions.doc: Takes the elements of the frames of `root` out of it, frees them, and lets the reference to `root` go. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_create
functions.doc: Creates an object of the type `type_id` ([`ferro_type_id`](crate::ferro_type_id)) with its default constructor and returns its handle, with one reference counted. `0` on a failure ([`ferro_last_error_code`](crate::ferro_last_error_code): [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] for an unknown ID, [`FERRO_NOT_SUPPORTED`] for a type without a default constructor, such as an abstract class). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_retain
functions.doc: Counts one more reference to `object`, which one more [`ferro_release`] gives back. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_release
functions.doc: Gives back one reference to `object`. When the last one is given back the handle is no longer valid; the object itself lives on while the framework holds it (a child in a panel, an open window). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_type_of
functions.doc: The type ID of the class of `object` (as [`ferro_type_id`](crate::ferro_type_id) gives it), or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_api_fingerprint
functions.doc: The fingerprint of the stable IDs of this library: the one of the API model it was built with (`bindings/model/ferroui-api.json`). A binding generated from the model compares it with its own at start; a different value means its ID constants are not the IDs of this library. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_selection_fingerprint
functions.doc: The fingerprint of the selection of classes and calls the library was built for (`scripts/capi/app_library.py`, docs/c-abi.md, section 17): `0` for a library of every class and call (the full and the by-use builds of the crate). A binding generated from the same selection has the same value (`selectionFingerprint()` of the Osprey bindings, `FERRO_APP_SELECTION_FINGERPRINT` of the C header the generator writes); a binding accepts a library whose value is `0` or its own. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_type_id
functions.doc: The type ID of the class named `name` (`Button`, or `FerroUI.Controls.Button` where two namespaces have a class of the name): a positive ID, or [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`]. `length` is the length of the name in bytes; a negative length means a NUL-terminated name. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_property_id
functions.doc: The property ID of the name `name` (`Text`, or `Grid.Row` for the property a class owns, attached properties included): a positive ID. The ID is the name: it is checked against a class when it is first used with an object of that class ([`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] then). `length` as for [`ferro_type_id`]. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_event_id
functions.doc: The event ID of the name `name` (`Click`): a routed event of the class of the object or of a base class, or an event its metadata declares; `Button.Click` is the routed event a class owns, for a handler on an ancestor of the objects that raise it. As for [`ferro_property_id`], the ID is the name, checked when it is first used with a class. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_table
functions.doc: Creates the signal table of the process with room for `capacity` slots (rounded up to a multiple of 64), or returns the one that exists (whose capacity then stays). The arrays stay at their addresses until the process ends. `NULL` on a failure (a capacity that is not positive or above 2^24; off the UI thread). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signals_init
functions.doc: [`ferro_signal_table`] for a language that cannot read memory (it calls `ferro_signal_set_*` and `ferro_signal_get_*`): creates the table, or keeps the one that exists, and returns a status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_new
functions.doc: Takes a free slot of the kind `kind` (`FERRO_SIGNAL_I64` to `FERRO_SIGNAL_TEXT`), with the value `0` (the empty text), and returns its index, or a negative status ([`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`] when the table is full or not created). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_free
functions.doc: Frees the slot `slot`: its bindings are removed and its kind is `FERRO_SIGNAL_FREE` until [`ferro_signal_new`] takes it again. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_set_i64
functions.doc: Writes an integer into the slot and marks it dirty (the store and the bit of section 14, for a language that cannot write memory). Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_set_f64
functions.doc: Writes a number into the slot and marks it dirty. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_set_bool
functions.doc: Writes a boolean into the slot and marks it dirty. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_set_handle
functions.doc: Writes a handle (`0` for null) into the slot and marks it dirty. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_set_str
functions.doc: Writes UTF-8 text (`length` bytes, negative for NUL-terminated) into a text slot and marks it dirty; the slot value becomes the length. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_get_i64
functions.doc: The integer of the slot (the load of section 14, for a language that cannot read memory); `0` when the slot is not an integer slot (recorded). Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_get_f64
functions.doc: The number of the slot; `0` when the slot is not a number slot (recorded). Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_get_bool
functions.doc: The boolean of the slot; `false` when the slot is not a boolean slot (recorded). Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_version
functions.doc: The version of the slot (raised every time its value changes); `-1` for a slot that is not in the table (recorded). Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_signal_get_cstr
functions.doc: The text of a text slot as NUL-terminated UTF-8 owned by the library until the next call on the thread; the empty text when the slot is not a text slot (recorded), never `NULL`. A language reads it when the version of the slot changed. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_bind
functions.doc: Binds `property` of `object` to the slot: the property takes the value of the slot now and every time an apply finds the slot dirty, with no frame and no call of the language. Returns a positive binding ID for [`ferro_signal_unbind`], or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_watch
functions.doc: Watches `property` of `object` into the slot: the library writes the value of the property into the slot now and every time it changes (the value, then the version, then the changed bit), so the language reads it with a load and no call. A text property goes into a text slot (read with [`ferro_signal_get_cstr`] when the version changed). Returns a positive binding ID for [`ferro_signal_unbind`], or a negative status. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_unbind
functions.doc: Removes a binding of [`ferro_signal_bind`] or [`ferro_signal_watch`]. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signals_apply
functions.doc: Applies the dirty slots: for each slot whose dirty bit is set, its version is raised and its value written to every property bound to it. Returns the number of slots applied, or a negative status (the first failed write; the others are still made). The library applies by itself at the start of every frame commit and at the end of every dispatch; a language calls this after writing slots outside them (a timer of its own). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_signal_take_changed
functions.doc: Clears `changed` bits of the slot for a language that cannot write memory, and returns whether it was set. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_init
functions.doc: Makes the calling thread the UI thread: UI objects can be created and used on it from now on, and on no other thread. Registers the tables of types, so that every type, property and event of the framework can be found by name. Calling it again on the UI thread does nothing; on another thread it returns [`FERRO_WRONG_THREAD`]. [`ferro_app_run`](crate::ferro_app_run) calls it, so an application that starts with `ferro_app_run` does not; a host that drives the thread itself (tests, an application of its own) calls it first. On macOS the UI thread of a desktop application is the main thread of the process.

functions.name: ferro_is_ui_thread
functions.doc: Whether the calling thread is the UI thread. Any thread.

functions.name: ferro_post
functions.doc: Runs `function(token)` on the UI thread, after the work already queued there, at the normal priority of the dispatcher. Any thread, the UI thread included (the work then runs later, not inside the call). Work that is still queued when the application ends does not run.

functions.name: ferro_post_data
functions.doc: [`ferro_post`] with a `void *` for the work in place of a token: runs `function(user_data)` on the UI thread once. Work that is still queued when the application ends does not run, and its user data is not released.

functions.name: ferro_run_jobs
functions.doc: Runs the work queued on the UI thread (posted work, timers that are due, layout and the other jobs of the dispatcher) and returns once the queue is empty: for a host that drives the UI thread itself instead of [`ferro_app_run`](crate::ferro_app_run). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_timer_start
functions.doc: Starts a timer on the UI thread: `function(token, elapsed)` is called every `interval` milliseconds (at least 1), on the UI thread, with the time since the previous tick (or since the start, for the first) in microseconds as `elapsed`. It returns `0` to go on ticking; any other result stops the timer. Returns a positive timer ID for [`ferro_timer_stop`], or a negative status. Timers tick while the main loop of [`ferro_app_run`](crate::ferro_app_run) runs, or in [`ferro_run_jobs`](crate::ferro_run_jobs) once they are due. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_timer_stop
functions.doc: Stops the timer `timer` ([`ferro_timer_start`]): its function is not called again. [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] for an ID that is not a running timer (one that stopped itself is gone after its last tick). It may be called from the function of the timer itself. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_add_child
functions.doc: Adds the control `child` to the children of `parent`: at the end of the `Children` of a panel or of the `Items` of an items control; as the one `Content` of a content control (a window) or of a content presenter, or the `Child` of a decorator or a popup, which must not hold one yet ([`FERRO_INVALID_STATE`]). The parent holds its own reference: the handle of the child can be released afterwards. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_remove_child
functions.doc: Removes the control `child` from the children of `parent` (see [`ferro_add_child`]); [`FERRO_NOT_FOUND`] if it is not one of them. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_str
functions.doc: Writes text to `property` of `object`: the text itself to a text property; the member of that name (in any case) to an enumeration; a value parsed from the text otherwise (a brush from `"Red"`, a thickness from `"4,2"`), or the text as the content of a content property. `length` is the length in bytes, a negative length means NUL-terminated. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_f64
functions.doc: Writes a number to `property` of `object`: straight to a `double` property, converted to any other numeric type. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_i64
functions.doc: Writes an integer to `property` of `object`: straight to an `int32_t` or `int64_t` property, the member with that numeric value to an enumeration (or the combination of bits to a set of flags), converted to any other numeric type. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_bool
functions.doc: Writes a boolean to `property` of `object`. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_handle
functions.doc: Writes an object to `property` of `object` (a `Content`, a `Child`, a brush object): `0` writes null. The property holds its own reference: the handle can be released afterwards. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_clear
functions.doc: Clears the local value of `property` of `object`, which then has its styled, inherited or default value again. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_f64
functions.doc: Reads a number from `property` of `object` into `*result`: a `double` property directly, any other numeric property converted. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_i64
functions.doc: Reads an integer from `property` of `object` into `*result`: an integer property, or the numeric value of the member of an enumeration. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_bool
functions.doc: Reads a boolean from `property` of `object` into `*result`. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_str
functions.doc: Reads the text of `property` of `object` (see [`ferro_set_str`]) as UTF-8 into `buffer`, with a NUL at the end, and its length in bytes (without the NUL) into `*length` when `length` is not `NULL`. When the text and its NUL do not fit in `capacity` bytes nothing is written to `buffer` and [`FERRO_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`] is returned, with the length written: a caller can ask for the length first with a `NULL` buffer and a capacity of `0`. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_cstr
functions.doc: Reads the text of `property` of `object` (see [`ferro_set_str`]) and returns it as a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string that the library owns: it stays valid until the next call of `ferro_get_cstr` on the thread, and the caller copies it to keep it. For a language whose strings are C strings and that cannot pass a buffer. `NULL` on a failure (a text with a NUL inside included: [`FERRO_INVALID_VALUE`]). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_handle
functions.doc: Reads the object held by `property` of `object` into `*result`: its handle with one more reference counted, which the caller releases ([`ferro_release`](crate::ferro_release)), or `0` for null. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_f64_or
functions.doc: Reads a number from `property` of `object`, as [`ferro_get_f64`] does, and returns it; returns `fallback` when the read fails (the failure is recorded: [`ferro_last_error`]). For a language that cannot pass a pointer to a result. UI thread only. [`ferro_last_error`]: crate::ferro_last_error

functions.name: ferro_get_i64_or
functions.doc: Reads an integer from `property` of `object`, as [`ferro_get_i64`] does, and returns it; returns `fallback` when the read fails (the failure is recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_bool_or
functions.doc: Reads a boolean from `property` of `object`, as [`ferro_get_bool`] does, and returns it; returns `fallback` when the read fails (the failure is recorded). UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_get_cstr_or
functions.doc: Reads the text of `property` of `object` as [`ferro_get_cstr`] does, and returns `fallback` (the caller's own string, returned as it is) in place of `NULL` when the read fails (the failure is recorded): for a language whose strings cannot be `NULL`. UI thread only.

functions.name: ferro_set_str16
functions.doc: Writes UTF-16 text (`units` code units) to `property` of `object`, as [`ferro_set_str`] does with UTF-8: for a language whose strings are UTF-16 (C#, Java, JavaScript), so that it passes its string without converting it. UI thread only.

FerroStartFn.doc: The start callback of [`ferro_app_run`]: called on the UI thread once the application is set up, with the token given to `ferro_app_run`. It returns `0` to run the main loop; any other value ends `ferro_app_run` with [`FERRO_START_FAILED`].

FerroEventFn.doc: The handler of an event ([`ferro_subscribe`]): called on the UI thread with the token of the subscription, the handle of the object the handler is attached to (borrowed for the call: [`ferro_retain`] it to keep it) and an argument (`0` for routed events in ABI version 1). A result other than `0` marks a routed event as handled.

FerroEventDataFn.doc: The handler of an event with user data ([`ferro_subscribe_data`]): as [`FerroEventFn`], with the user data in place of the token.

FerroReleaseFn.doc: Releases the user data of a subscription ([`ferro_subscribe_data`]) once the handler is removed: by [`ferro_unsubscribe`], or when the object goes away.

FerroCreateFn.doc: Called once for every new instance of a class, with the data of the class ([`ferro_class_set_data`]) and the instance (borrowed for the call); the callback gives the instance its own data with [`ferro_object_set_data`].

FerroRenderFn.doc: Render: `context` names the drawing context of the call for the `ferro_draw_*` functions; it is valid until the callback returns.

FerroNotifyFn.doc: A notification with one integer: a property of the class changed (`arg` is its property ID), the instance was attached to or detached from the visual tree, its template was applied.

FerroReleaseDataFn.doc: Called when an instance goes away, with its data, so that the language releases it.

FerroPostFn.doc: Work posted to the UI thread with [`ferro_post`]: called with its token. The result is ignored (a function that returns `int64_t` is what every language can make).

FerroPostDataFn.doc: Work posted to the UI thread with [`ferro_post_data`]: called once with its user data.

FerroTimerFn.doc: The function of a timer ([`ferro_timer_start`]): called on the UI thread with the token of the timer and the time since its previous tick (or its start) in microseconds. It returns `0` to go on ticking; any other value stops the timer.

statuses.doc: The call succeeded.

statuses.name: FERRO_ERROR
statuses.doc: A failure that no other code describes; the message says what happened.

statuses.name: FERRO_INVALID_ARGUMENT

statuses.name: FERRO_INVALID_UTF8
statuses.doc: A string argument is not UTF-8.

statuses.doc: No type, property or event has the name or ID.

statuses.name: FERRO_BAD_HANDLE
statuses.doc: The handle is `0`, was released, or was never issued.

statuses.doc: The function was called on a thread that is not the UI thread.

classes.name: AcrylicBrush
classes.doc: A brush that paints the acrylic material of WinUI (WinUI `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.AcrylicBrush`): what is behind the element, blurred, with its luminosity taken from a luminosity colour and its colour from the tint, and a little noise; or, when the tint is opaque, the tint with noise. The brush falls back to its [`fallback_color`](XamlCompositionBrushBase::fallback_color) when [`always_use_fallback`](Self::always_use_fallback) is set or the [`MaterialPolicy`] disables materials (energy saver, transparency effects off), cross-fading over 167 ms. With the [`background_source`](Self::background_source) `HostBackdrop` (WinUI 2's window acrylic) it shows what is behind the window, and also falls back while no window of the application is active; in a window the platform shows nothing behind (an opaque window) it paints its fallback colour. A value of -1 (the default) leaves that dimension out; with both at -1 the trigger never applies.

classes.doc: Encapsulates a FerroUI application. The [`Application`] class encapsulates application-specific functionality, including: - A global set of [`data_templates`](Application::data_templates). - A global set of [`styles`](Application::styles). - An input manager. - Registers services needed by the rest of the framework in the [`register_services`](Application::register_services) method. - Tracks the lifetime of the application. An application class derives from it and overrides the members of [`ApplicationImpl`]: ```ignore #[repr(C)] pub struct App { base: Application } ferro_class!(App: Application); ferro_impl_classes!(App: FerroObjectImpl); impl ApplicationImpl for App { fn initialize(this: &Self) { this.styles().add(theme()); } } impl NewApplication for App { fn new_application() -> Ref<Self> { instantiate(Self { base: Application::construct() }) } } ```

classes.doc: A text box with a list of suggestions the application supplies (WinUI's `AutoSuggestBox`). The application listens to `TextChanged`, raised 150 ms after the last change of the text with its reason, and sets the items (or `ItemsSource`) to the suggestions; the box shows them in a popup while it has the focus. Choosing a suggestion with the arrow keys or the pointer raises `SuggestionChosen` (and puts its text, by `TextMemberPath`, in the box when `UpdateTextOnSelect` is set); Enter, a click of a suggestion and the query button raise `QuerySubmitted`. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/AutoSuggestBox.xaml`, from WinUI's `DefaultAutoSuggestBoxStyle`), with WinUI's parts: the text box `TextBox`, the popup `SuggestionsPopup` with `SuggestionsContainer` and the list `SuggestionsList`, and the button `QueryButton`. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): `AutoMaximizeSuggestionArea`, `LightDismissOverlayMode`, `TextBoxStyle`, `HeaderPlacement`, the input validation of WinUI and the placement of the list above the box when there is no room below.

classes.name: Calendar
classes.doc: Represents a control that enables a user to select a date by using a visual calendar display. A Calendar control can be used on its own, or as a drop-down part of a date picker control. A Calendar displays either the days of a month, the months of a year, or the years of a decade, depending on the value of the DisplayMode property.  When displaying the days of a month, the user can select a date, a range of dates, or multiple ranges of dates.  The kinds of selections that are allowed are controlled by the SelectionMode property. The range of dates displayed is governed by the DisplayDateStart and DisplayDateEnd properties.  If DisplayMode is Year or Decade, only months or years that contain displayable dates will be displayed. The BlackoutDates property can be used to specify dates that cannot be selected. These dates will be displayed as dimmed and disabled. By default, Today is highlighted.  This can be disabled by setting IsTodayHighlighted to false. The Calendar control provides basic navigation using either the mouse or keyboard. The following table summarizes keyboard navigation. ```text Key Combination     DisplayMode     Action ARROW               Any             Change focused date, unselect all selected dates, and select new focused date. SHIFT+ARROW         Any             If SelectionMode is not set to SingleDate or None begin selecting a range of dates. CTRL+UP ARROW       Any             Switch to the next larger DisplayMode.  If DisplayMode is already Decade, no action. CTRL+DOWN ARROW     Any             Switch to the next smaller DisplayMode.  If DisplayMode is already Month, no action. SPACEBAR            Month           Select focused date. SPACEBAR            Year or Decade  Switch DisplayMode to the Month or Year represented by focused item. ```

classes.name: FontIcon
classes.doc: Represents an icon that uses a glyph of a font as its content (WinUI's `FontIcon`). The template of the theme draws [`glyph`](Self::glyph) in its text part `PART_Text` with the font family, size, style, weight and foreground of the icon. The size is 20 by default, as in WinUI; the font family is the theme resource `SymbolThemeFontFamily` (Segoe Fluent Icons in the WinUI theme), set by the theme, where WinUI takes it from the default font of a font icon. The font is not bundled: off Windows an application supplies a symbol font and sets `SymbolThemeFontFamily` or the icon's `FontFamily` (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.2). The WinUI theme has the template; the Fluent and Simple themes have none. Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, FontIcon): `IsTextScaleFactorEnabled` (FerroUI has no text scale factor).

classes.name: FontIconSource
classes.doc: The description of a [`FontIcon`] (WinUI's `FontIconSource`). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, FontIcon): `IsTextScaleFactorEnabled`.

classes.name: Frame
classes.doc: A content control that navigates between pages of the WinUI model (WinUI's `Frame`): it shows a [`FramePage`] of the type of a navigation and keeps a journal of the pages it showed (the back and the forward stack) and a cache of pages (`CacheSize`, `FramePage::navigation_cache_mode`). A navigation is synchronous: `navigate`, `go_back` and `go_forward` raise `Navigating`, which can cancel it, call the callbacks of the old and the new page, raise `Navigated`, and return; a navigation requested by one of those handlers while the frame navigates is ignored. The type of a page is a [`PageType`] (`PageType::of::<MyPage>()`, WinUI's `TypeName`); a page is created by the page factory registered for its type (`register_page_factory`) or by the default constructor the page type carries. The upstream pages (`Page`, `NavigationPage`) are another model; docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 7, compares them. The WinUI theme has the template (WinUI's `Frame` style of `generic.xaml`); the Fluent and Simple themes have none. Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.4): the navigation transitions (`ContentTransitions`, the `NavigationTransitionInfo` of `Navigate`), `GetNavigationState` and `SetNavigationState`.

classes.name: FramePage
classes.doc: A page a [`Frame`] navigates to (WinUI's `Page`, a `UserControl`). The name keeps `Page` for the upstream page of `ferroui-controls` ([`crate::Page`], a templated control with asynchronous navigation); the two navigation models are separate (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 7). A derived page overrides the callbacks of [`FramePageImpl`] (`on_navigated_to`, `on_navigating_from`, `on_navigated_from`), which the frame calls synchronously. The page is styled as a `UserControl` (WinUI's `Page` has no style of its own). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.4): `TopAppBar`, `BottomAppBar` and the navigation transitions of the page.

The source holds its elements weakly and does not subscribe to them, so neither keeps the other alive. This class is abstract: it creates no element ([`create_icon_element`] is `None`, as WinUI's base returns no element); the derived sources create theirs. classes.name: InfoBadge
classes.doc: A small badge that draws attention to an item (WinUI's `InfoBadge`): a dot, an icon or a number. A [`value`](Self::value) of 0 or more is shown as a number and takes precedence over the [`icon_source`](Self::icon_source); with the value -1 (the default) the badge shows the icon of its icon source, and a dot without one. The control sets the states of WinUI as pseudo-classes, which the control theme of the WinUI theme (`src/FerroUI.Themes.WinUI/Controls/InfoBadge.xaml`) styles: `:dot`, `:icon`, `:font-icon` (an icon of a [`FontIconSource`]) and `:value` (DisplayKindStates). The template binds the number to [`value`](Self::value) and the icon and the corner radius to the [`template_settings`](Self::template_settings). The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Differences from WinUI (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.2): a value below -1 is coerced to -1 and logged, where WinUI throws; whether `CornerRadius` is local is followed from the priority of its changes.

classes.name: InfoBadgeTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values the template of an [`InfoBadge`](crate::InfoBadge) binds to: the corner radius of the badge (half its height unless the badge has a local `CornerRadius`) and the icon element created from its `IconSource`. Each badge has its own.

classes.name: InfoBar
classes.doc: An inline message of the application (WinUI's `InfoBar`): a title, a message, an action button and content, with the icon and the colours of its [`severity`](Self::severity), shown while [`is_open`](Self::is_open) and closed by its close button or by the application. The control sets the states of WinUI as pseudo-classes, which the control theme of the WinUI theme (`src/FerroUI.Themes.WinUI/Controls/InfoBar.xaml`) styles: `:informational`, `:success`, `:warning`, `:error` (SeverityLevels), `:standard-icon-visible`, `:user-icon-visible` (IconStates; neither is NoIconVisible), `:close-button-collapsed`, `:open` (InfoBarVisible; its absence is InfoBarCollapsed), `:foreground-set` (a `Foreground` set on the bar itself) and `:no-banner-content` (no title, message or action button). The template parts it looks up are the button `CloseButton` and the severity icon `StandardIcon`; the content is presented by `PART_ContentPresenter` (WinUI's `ContentArea`). The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Differences from WinUI (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.2): the bar is a [`ContentControl`]; UI Automation notifications are not raised (the peer reports the title and the message as the name and a live setting of the severity instead); the texts of the close button and the severity icons are WinUI's English texts.

classes.name: InfoBarAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of an [`InfoBar`]: a status bar, as in WinUI. WinUI raises UI Automation notifications when the bar opens and closes (`RaiseNotificationEvent` with the text of the severity, the title and the message), which FerroUI's automation has no counterpart of. The peer exposes the bar instead: its name is the title and the message of the bar when the application gives it none, it raises a change of the name when they change, and its live setting is assertive for warnings and errors and polite otherwise when the application sets none (WinUI's processing of the notifications, `GetProcessingForSeverity`).

classes.name: InfoBarPanel
classes.doc: Lays out its children on one line when they fit in its width, and below each other otherwise (`InfoBarPanel` of WinUI). One line: the children side by side, each moved by its `HorizontalOrientationMargin` (the left margin of the first and the right margin of the last left out), the last one given the rest of the width, the panel padded by `HorizontalOrientationPadding`. Below each other: each child moved by its `VerticalOrientationMargin` (the top margin of the first and the bottom margin of the last left out), the panel padded by `VerticalOrientationPadding`. A child without a width or a height (a collapsed one) is left out of both. One child, children wider than the panel, or a child that would be taller on one line than the minimum height of the parent of the panel (less the vertical margins of the panel) give the layout below each other.

classes.name: InfoBarTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values the template of an [`InfoBar`](crate::InfoBar) binds to: the icon element created from its `IconSource` (`TemplateSettings.IconElement`, the child of the `UserIconBox` of the template). Each bar has its own.

classes.name: InteractiveBurningFlameEffect
classes.doc: The burning flame as an interactive effect class (Effector's `BurningFlameShaderEffect`, the burn-away button): a press ignites the flame where it is (the height clamped to 0.18..0.92 of the host) at full strength, a drag while pressed moves the ignition, and after the release the flame burns down over 2.6 seconds; the phase of its waves and its strength advance on the frames of the animation clock ([`advance`](Self::advance)). It takes handled events: the host of the burn-away button is a button, whose own handler handles the press. Its value is a [`BurningFlameShaderEffect`].

classes.name: InteractivePointerSpotlightEffect

Its value is a [`PointerSpotlightShaderEffect`]: the radius, the strengths and the colour are set on it ([`set_value`](Self::set_value), [`update`](Self::update)), the pointer state is the class's.

classes.name: InteractiveReactiveGridEffect
classes.doc: The reactive grid as an interactive effect class (Effector's `ReactiveGridShaderEffect`): the halo follows the pointer over the host, and the host captures the pointer while it is pressed. Its value is a [`ReactiveGridShaderEffect`].

classes.name: InteractiveWaterRippleEffect
classes.doc: The water ripple as an interactive effect class (Effector's `WaterRippleShaderEffect`): a press makes a strong ripple where it is and captures the pointer, a drag makes weaker ones along the way (at least about a tenth of the host apart), the release one more; the ripples age on the frames of the animation clock until they are gone ([`advance`](Self::advance)). Its value is a [`WaterRippleShaderEffect`].

classes.name: NavigationView
classes.doc: A navigation pane with menu items and a content area (WinUI's `NavigationView`). The pane is at the left (`Left`, `LeftCompact`, `LeftMinimal`, or chosen by the width in `Auto`: the display modes `Expanded`, `Compact` and `Minimal`) or at the top (`Top`). The template of the WinUI theme is WinUI's (`NavigationView.xaml`): the control finds WinUI's parts (`RootSplitView`, `TogglePaneButton`, `NavigationViewBackButton`, `NavigationViewCloseButton`, `PaneAutoSuggestButton`, `PaneTitleTextBlock`, `PaneTitleHolder`, `PaneTitlePresenter`, `PaneTitleOnTopPane`, `MenuItemsHost`, `FooterMenuItemsHost`, `TopNavMenuItemsHost`, `TopFooterMenuItemsHost`, the content controls of the pane header, custom content, footer and auto suggest box of the left and the top pane, `ContentLeftPadding`), sets their contents and the values of [`template_settings`](Self::template_settings) as WinUI's code does, and sets WinUI's visual states as pseudo-classes (`:compact`, `:expanded`, `:minimal`, `:top-navigation-minimal`, `:minimal-with-back-button`, `:toggle-pane-button-visible`, `:header-collapsed`, `:auto-suggest-box-collapsed`, `:closed-compact`, `:list-size-compact`, `:pane-not-overlaying`, `:back-button-collapsed`, `:pane-collapsed`, and `:back-button-row-visible` for the row WinUI sizes in code). The Fluent and Simple themes have no template. The menu items are realized in stack panels, not in `ItemsRepeater`s with a hierarchical `SelectionModel` (follow-up F1). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.4): the overflow of the top pane, the animations of the pane, the shadow of the pane, the padding of the title bar, the shoulder navigation and the selectors of templates and styles.

classes.name: NavigationViewAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`NavigationView`]: the selection pattern over its realized containers, as WinUI's peer. The peer holds its owner weakly.

classes.name: NavigationViewItem
classes.doc: A selectable item of a [`NavigationView`](crate::NavigationView), with an icon, an info badge and child items (WinUI's `NavigationViewItem`). The template of the WinUI theme draws the item as WinUI's item presenter does (`NavigationViewItemPresenter` and its styles for the left and the top pane, folded into the template of the item). The item sets the states of WinUI as pseudo-classes: `:selected`, `:pressed`, `:on-top-navigation-primary`, `:icon-collapsed`, `:icon-only`, `:content-only`, `:info-badge-collapsed`, `:chevron-visible-open`, `:chevron-visible-closed` and `:closed-compact-and-top-level-item`. The child items are hosted in the template part `NavigationViewItemMenuItemsHost`, below the item, or in the popup `ChildrenFlyout` when the item is in the top pane or at the top level of a closed compact pane, as WinUI moves its repeater into its flyout. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template. The children are realized in a stack panel, not an `ItemsRepeater` (follow-up F1); the containers of data items are reused across edits of the collections.

classes.name: NavigationViewItemAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`NavigationViewItem`]: a list item (a tab item in the top pane) with the selection item pattern and, for an item with children, the expand and collapse pattern; like WinUI's peer at the pin it has no invoke pattern.

classes.name: NavigationViewItemBase
classes.doc: The base of the items of a [`NavigationView`](crate::NavigationView): their content and selection (WinUI's `NavigationViewItemBase`). As in WinUI, it cannot be created in markup.

classes.name: NavigationViewItemHeader
classes.doc: A heading of a group of items of a [`NavigationView`](crate::NavigationView) (WinUI's `NavigationViewItemHeader`). It is not focusable or enabled, as WinUI's style sets. The control sets WinUI's states as pseudo-classes: `:header-text-collapsed` (a top level header of a closed compact pane) and `:top-mode` (the top pane). The template of the WinUI theme presents the content in the text block `HeaderText`; the part `NavigationViewItemHeaderRootGrid` is indented by the depth of the header.

classes.name: NavigationViewItemSeparator
classes.doc: A line between items of a [`NavigationView`](crate::NavigationView) (WinUI's `NavigationViewItemSeparator`). It is not focusable or enabled, as WinUI's style sets. The control sets WinUI's states as pseudo-classes: `:horizontal-line-compact` (a closed compact pane) and `:vertical-line` (the top pane); the part `NavigationViewItemSeparatorRootGrid` is indented by the depth of the separator.

classes.name: NavigationViewTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values the template of a [`NavigationView`](crate::NavigationView) binds to (`TemplateSettings`), which the navigation view sets. Each navigation view has its own. WinUI's `Visibility` values are `bool`s here (`true` is `Visible`), as the `IsVisible` they are bound to.

classes.name: NotificationCard

classes.name: NumberBox
classes.doc: A text box for numbers (WinUI's `NumberBox`): a value of type `f64`, NaN when the box is empty, with a range, steps, wrapping, expressions and spin buttons. The text is committed when the box loses the focus, on Enter and before a step: it is parsed with the [`NumberFormatter`](Self::number_formatter_property), or evaluated as an expression (`utils::number_expression`) when [`AcceptsExpression`](Self::accepts_expression_property) is set. Up and Down (and the spin buttons and the mouse wheel) step by `SmallChange`, PageUp and PageDown by `LargeChange`; Escape restores the text of the value. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/NumberBox.xaml`, from WinUI's `NumberBox.xaml`), with WinUI's parts: the text box `InputBox`, the spin buttons `UpSpinButton` and `DownSpinButton`, the popup `UpDownPopup` with `PopupUpSpinButton` and `PopupDownSpinButton`, and `HeaderContentPresenter`. The control sets WinUI's visual states as pseudo-classes: `:spinbuttonsvisible` and `:spinbuttonspopup` (SpinButtonStates; neither is SpinButtonsCollapsed), `:upspinbuttondisabled` and `:downspinbuttondisabled`. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): `InputScope`, `SelectionFlyout`, `SelectionHighlightColor`, `TextReadingOrder` and `PreventKeyboardDisplayOnProgrammaticFocus`.

classes.name: NumberBoxAutomationPeer
classes.doc: An automation peer which represents a [`NumberBox`]: a spinner with the range value pattern, named by its header when it has no name. Deviation (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): WinUI's peer raises the change of `Value` only; this one also raises the changes of `Minimum`, `Maximum`, `SmallChange` and `LargeChange` (the identifiers of W1), as the range peers of the framework do.

classes.name: NumericUpDown
classes.doc: Control that represents a text box with button spinners that allow incrementing and decrementing numeric values.

classes.name: NumericUpDownAutomationPeer

classes.doc: A top-level over an offscreen implementation: laid out and rendered without a window of the platform.

classes.name: OverlayPopupHost

classes.name: Page
classes.doc: Abstract base class for all page types.

classes.name: PageNavigationHost
classes.doc: Hosts a page as the root of a top-level: forwards the safe-area padding and the system back navigation of the top-level to the page.

classes.name: PageStackEntry
classes.doc: An entry of the journal of a [`Frame`]: the type of a page and the parameter of its navigation. The parameter is kept as it is (by identity), as in WinUI. Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.4): `NavigationTransitionInfo`, FerroUI's frame has no navigation transitions.

classes.name: PagerControl
classes.doc: A control to move through the pages of a paged content (WinUI's `PagerControl`): buttons to the first, previous, next and last page around a combo box of the page numbers, a number box to type one, or a button for each page (`DisplayMode`). `NumberOfPages` is -1 while the number of pages is not known; `SelectedPageIndex` is the index of the page, from 0, kept in the range of the pages, and its changes raise `SelectedIndexChanged`. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/PagerControl.xaml`, from WinUI's `PagerControl.xaml`), with WinUI's parts `FirstPageButton`, `PreviousPageButton`, `NextPageButton`, `LastPageButton`, `ComboBoxDisplay`, `NumberBoxDisplay`, `NumberPanelItemsRepeater` and `NumberPanelCurrentPageIndicator`. The control sets WinUI's visual states as pseudo-classes: `:numberbox`, `:combobox` and `:numberpanel` (the display mode), `:infinite` (InfiniteItems), and for each button `:<button>collapsed`, `:<button>hidden` and `:<button>disabled` (`:firstcollapsed`, `:nexthidden`, ...). The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Differences (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, G2): the number panel is an items control whose panel is a horizontal stack panel, where WinUI has an `ItemsRepeater` with a `StackLayout` (`ferroui-controls` cannot depend on the repeater crate); the indicator of the current page moves without WinUI's `RepositionThemeTransition`.

classes.name: PagerControlAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`PagerControl`]: a menu with the selection pattern, as in WinUI. The selection is empty, as WinUI's `GetSelection` returns it: the number panel mixes buttons and ellipses, so the index of an element is not the index of a page. A change of the selected page invalidates the selection pattern (WinUI's `SelectionPatternOnInvalidated`), which FerroUI's automation reports as a change of its `Selection` property.

classes.name: PagerControlTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values the template of a [`PagerControl`](crate::PagerControl) binds to: the page numbers of its combo box (`Pages`, 1 to the number of pages) and the buttons and ellipses of its number panel (`NumberPanelItems`). Each pager has its own; the pager fills them.

classes.doc: Base class for controls that can contain multiple children. Controls can be added to a panel by adding them to its `children` collection. All children are layed out to fill the panel.

classes.name: PathIconSource

classes.name: PathSegment

classes.name: Pen

classes.name: PersonPicture
classes.doc: A picture of a person or a group (WinUI's `PersonPicture`): the profile picture, else the initials of the display name or of the contact, else the glyph of a contact, in a circle, with a badge (a number, a glyph or an image) at its top right. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/PersonPicture.xaml`, from WinUI's `PersonPicture.xaml`), with WinUI's parts `InitialsTextBlock`, `BadgeNumberTextBlock`, `BadgeGlyphIcon`, `BadgingEllipse` and `BadgingBackgroundEllipse`. The control sets WinUI's visual states as pseudo-classes: `:photo`, `:nophotoorinitials` and `:group` (CommonStates; Initials sets none), `:badge` and `:badgeimage` (BadgeStates). It keeps itself a circle: a change of its size sets its width and height to the smaller of them, as WinUI's does. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Differences (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 10.10): the contact is FerroUI's [`Contact`], whose pictures are images, so the picture of a contact is shown at once (WinUI opens and decodes a stream reference asynchronously, at the size of the control); the pictures are image brush sources (a bitmap), the type of the image brush that paints them.

classes.name: PersonPictureAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`PersonPicture`]: text, whose name is the automation name the picture sets (the person and the badge), as in WinUI.

classes.name: PersonPictureTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values the template of a [`PersonPicture`](crate::PersonPicture) binds to: the initials it shows and the brush of its picture. Each picture has its own; the picture sets them.

classes.name: PickerPresenterBase
classes.doc: Defines the base class for the date and time picker presenters.

classes.name: PinchGestureRecognizer
classes.doc: Recognizes the pinch gesture: two contacts moving closer together or further apart, and rotating around each other.

classes.name: PipsPager
classes.doc: Represents a control that lets the user navigate through a paginated collection using a set of pips.

classes.name: PipsPagerAutomationPeer

classes.name: PipsPagerTemplateSettings

classes.name: Pivot
classes.doc: A control that shows one of its items at a time, under a row of headers that the user taps, pans or flicks through (WinUI's `Pivot`). The items are [`PivotItem`]s (other items get one as their container). The pivot keeps one item selected while it has items ([`SelectionMode::ALWAYS_SELECTED`]); setting [`selected_index`](SelectingItemsControl::selected_index) flies the current item out and the new one in, a pan of the content moves to the neighbour past a quarter of the width. With [`is_header_items_carousel_enabled`](Self::is_header_items_carousel_enabled) (the default) the headers and the items wrap around. [`is_locked`](Self::is_locked) keeps the selected item. The structure is WinUI's (decision D8): the items are in a `ScrollViewer` (template part `ScrollViewer`) whose content is a [`PivotPanel`] (`Panel`) a thousand sections wide, kept near its middle by the pivot's state machine; the panel holds the `PivotLayoutElement` with the headers and the `PivotItemPresenter`. During a pan the layout element stays in the viewport and the items follow the content through expression animations of their `Translation`, on the compositor (WinUI's secondary content relationships).

classes.name: PivotAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`Pivot`]: a Tab with the Selection pattern.

classes.name: PivotHeaderItem
classes.doc: A header of a [`Pivot`] (WinUI's `PivotHeaderItem`): the pivot makes one per item, its content bound to the item's header. Its selection state is WinUI's: `Disabled`, `Selected`, `SelectedPointerOver`, `SelectedPressed`, `Unselected`, `UnselectedPointerOver`, `UnselectedPressed` and `UnselectedLocked` (the pivot is locked). The states are shown through the pseudo-classes `:selected`, `:pressed` and `:locked` (with `:pointerover` and `:disabled`), as the other WinUI controls of the theme (decision D2), and a template with visual state groups gets the state by name through the visual state manager.

classes.name: PivotHeaderPanel
classes.doc: The panel of the headers of a [`Pivot`] (WinUI's `PivotHeaderPanel`, a `Canvas`): the headers side by side, starting at the header of the selected item at the current offset, so that the selected header comes first and the headers before it follow at the end. The pivot moves the panel with the parallax of its scroll viewer.

classes.name: PivotItem
classes.doc: An item of a [`Pivot`] (WinUI's `PivotItem`): a content control with the [`header`](Self::header) the pivot shows for it. The pivot shows one item at a time (and its neighbours while it is panned): the others are transparent, not hit testable, and the root of their template is collapsed so that tabbing skips them (WinUI's `SetContentVisibility`).

classes.name: PivotItemAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`PivotItem`]: a TabItem with the SelectionItem pattern.

classes.name: PivotPanel
classes.doc: The panel inside the scroll viewer of a [`Pivot`] (WinUI's `PivotPanel`): as wide as [`PIVOT_PANEL_MULTIPLIER`] sections while the headers wrap, with a regular snap point at every section, so that the scroll viewer pans one section at a time. Its child named `PivotLayoutElement` (the headers and the items) is measured and arranged one section wide. WinUI arranges it at the start of the panel and keeps it in the viewport with a secondary content relationship of the scroll viewer; here it is arranged at the section the viewport rests on (the pivot's section offset), and the pivot's composition expression keeps it in place during a pan (a recorded deviation: layout and hit testing stay where the content is shown at rest).

classes.name: PlatformGeometry
classes.doc: A geometry that wraps a platform implementation.

classes.name: PointAnimation
classes.doc: Animates a [`Point`] property (WinUI's `PointAnimation`). It animates from `From` (or the value the property has when it begins) to `To`, or by `By` from the start; with neither `To` nor `By` it animates back to the value of the property without animations. `EasingFunction` eases the progress. `EnableDependentAnimation` is accepted and has no effect: every property is animated on the UI thread.

classes.name: PointAnimationUsingKeyFrames
classes.doc: Animates a `Point` property through its `KeyFrames` (WinUI's `PointAnimationUsingKeyFrames`). Before the first key frame the value goes from the value the property has when the animation begins; after the last it holds the last value. With an automatic `Duration` the animation lasts until its last key time. `EnableDependentAnimation` is accepted and has no effect.

classes.name: PointKeyFrame
classes.doc: The base class of the key frames of a `Point` property (WinUI's `PointKeyFrame`): a `Value` reached at a `KeyTime`.

classes.name: PolyLineSegment

classes.name: Polygon

classes.name: Polyline

classes.name: PolylineGeometry
classes.doc: Represents the geometry of a polyline or polygon.

classes.doc: A control used to indicate the progress of an operation.

classes.name: ProgressBarAutomationPeer
classes.doc: An automation peer which represents a progress bar.

classes.name: ProgressBarTemplateSettings
classes.doc: Provides calculated values for use with the [`ProgressBar`]'s control theme or template. This class is NOT intended for general use outside of control templates.

classes.name: ProgressRing
classes.doc: A ring that shows that something is in progress (WinUI's `ProgressRing`): a spinning arc while [`is_indeterminate`](Self::is_indeterminate) (the default), the part of a ring of the [`value`](Self::value) between [`minimum`](Self::minimum) and [`maximum`](Self::maximum) otherwise, and nothing while not [`is_active`](Self::is_active). As in WinUI, `Value`, `Minimum` and `Maximum` are properties of the ring (not of `RangeBase`), coerced as `ProgressRing.cpp` coerces them: the bound set last wins, and a value outside the range is moved into it. The control sets the states of WinUI as pseudo-classes, which the control theme of the WinUI theme (`src/FerroUI.Themes.WinUI/Controls/ProgressRing.xaml`) styles: `:active` (Active), `:determinate-active` (DeterminateActive) and `:inactive` (Inactive). WinUI draws the ring with an `AnimatedVisualPlayer` and the Lottie compositions of its animated visuals, which the code plays. FerroUI has no player: the template draws the ring with `Arc` shapes, and the control moves the arc of the template part `PART_Indicator` as the code of WinUI plays the compositions: the indeterminate composition loops over two seconds (the arc grows to half the ring and shrinks while it turns 900 degrees), and a determinate change plays the determinate composition from the old to the new value (two seconds for the whole ring), a decrease at once. The clock is the ring's `Clock`, or the global clock; the motion stops while the ring is inactive, hidden or out of the visual tree. `DeterminateSource` and `IndeterminateSource` (preview members of WinUI) are not ported. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1).

classes.name: ProgressRingAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The automation peer of a [`ProgressRing`]: a progress bar with the range value pattern while the ring is determinate, as in WinUI. The name of an active indeterminate ring starts with "Busy".

classes.name: ProgressRingTemplateSettings
classes.doc: The values of the template of a [`ProgressRing`](crate::ProgressRing) that WinUI keeps for the templates of the earlier ProgressRing of Windows (read-only): the diameter and the offset of its ellipses and the side of the ring, from the actual width of the ring.

classes.name: QuadraticBezierSegment

classes.name: QuadraticEase
classes.doc: The curve `t^2` (WinUI's `QuadraticEase`).

classes.name: QuarticEase
classes.doc: The curve `t^4` (WinUI's `QuarticEase`).

classes.name: QuinticEase
classes.doc: The curve `t^5` (WinUI's `QuinticEase`).

classes.name: RadialGradientBrush
classes.doc: Paints an area with a radial gradient.

classes.name: RadioButton
classes.doc: Represents a button that allows a user to select a single option from a group of options.

classes.name: RadioButtonAutomationPeer
classes.doc: An automation peer which represents a [`RadioButton`].

classes.name: RadioButtons
classes.doc: A group of radio buttons with one selection (WinUI's `RadioButtons`). The items are shown as [`RadioButton`]s: an item that is a radio button is its own container, and another item is the content of a radio button. The selection is the selection of the items control (`SelectedIndex`, `SelectedItem`, `SelectionChanged`), kept with the checked state of the containers. The arrow keys move the focus and the selection within the group without wrapping, Tab enters the group at the selected button, and Ctrl with an arrow key moves the focus only. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/RadioButtons.xaml`, from WinUI's `RadioButtons.xaml`), with the parts `PART_HeaderPresenter` and `PART_ItemsPresenter` (WinUI's `HeaderContentPresenter` and the `ItemsRepeater` `InnerRepeater`); the theme sets the items panel, a [`RadioButtonsPanel`](crate::primitives::RadioButtonsPanel) with the spacing of the resources `RadioButtonsColumnSpacing` and `RadioButtonsRowSpacing`. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). The exclusive check is the radio button group manager's: the containers are the logical children of the group and have no group name, so checking one unchecks the others. The group itself only checks the container of a new selection, and unchecks the container of the old one when no container is checked instead (a cleared selection, or one whose container is not realized), which the group manager never does (WinUI's `Select` writes both containers). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): WinUI's element factories and `DataTemplateSelector` as `ItemTemplate`.

classes.name: RadioButtonsAutomationPeer
classes.doc: An automation peer which represents a [`RadioButtons`]: a group named by its header when it has no name. Deviation (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): WinUI's peer is a plain group; this one is the peer of a selecting items control, with the selection pattern of the group.

classes.name: RadioButtonsPanel
classes.doc: Lays out the radio buttons of a [`RadioButtons`] in columns of equal cells as large as the largest one, filling each column from the top, with as many columns as the available width and the `MaxColumns` of the group allow (WinUI's `ColumnMajorUniformToLargestGridLayout`). Deviation (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): WinUI lays the buttons out with a layout of an `ItemsRepeater`; FerroUI's `RadioButtons` is an items control, and this panel is its items panel, set by the control theme of the WinUI theme with the spacing of the resources `RadioButtonsColumnSpacing` and `RadioButtonsRowSpacing`. `MaxColumns` is read from the group the panel is the items panel of (its templated parent); a panel of another control has one column.

classes.name: RangeBase
classes.doc: Base class for controls that display a value within a range. This class is abstract: only its subclasses can be created.

classes.name: RangeBaseAutomationPeer
classes.doc: The base class of the automation peers which represent a [`RangeBase`].

classes.name: RatingControl
classes.doc: A control to rate with stars (WinUI's `RatingControl`): a value from 1 to `MaxRating`, or -1 while it is not set, a placeholder value (a community rating) shown while it is not set, and a caption. The items are drawn twice, in the background stack panel in the unset state and in the foreground stack panel clipped to the value, from the glyphs of a [`RatingItemFontInfo`] (the stars E735 and E734 of the symbol font by default, in the font of the control) or the images of a [`RatingItemImageInfo`]. A click or a tap sets the rating under the pointer, and clears it when it is the rating (with `IsClearEnabled`); the arrow keys, Home and End change it. Only the changes of the user raise `ValueChanged`. The template is the control theme of the WinUI theme (`Controls/RatingControl.xaml`, from WinUI's `RatingControl.xaml`), with WinUI's parts `RatingBackgroundStackPanel` and `RatingForegroundStackPanel`; the items take their size from the `FontSize` of the stack panels (`RatingControlFontSizeForRendering`) and their brushes from the theme. The control sets WinUI's visual states (CommonStates) as the pseudo-classes `:placeholder`, `:pointeroverplaceholder`, `:pointeroverunselected`, `:set` and `:pointeroverset` (Disabled is `:disabled`). The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). Missing (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, Input): the composition animations of the scale of the items (the scale is set when the pointer moves), and the focus engagement of the gamepad (`IsFocusEngagementEnabled`, GamepadA and GamepadB).

classes.name: StateTriggerBase
classes.doc: The base class of the triggers of a [`VisualState`](super::VisualState): while a trigger of a state is active, the state is a candidate to be the current state of its group (docs/porting/winui-calculator-gaps.md, section 5.7). **The extension point of custom triggers.** A trigger of an application derives from this class and calls [`set_active`](Self::set_active) when its condition changes (WinUI's protected `SetActive`; it is public in Rust, which has no protected members, and is meant for the derived trigger only): ```ignore #[repr(C)] pub struct ControlSizeTrigger { base: StateTriggerBase, /* ... */ } ferro_class!(ControlSizeTrigger: StateTriggerBase); // ... on a size change of the source: trigger.set_active(size.width >= trigger.min_width()); ``` Among the states of a group whose triggers are active, a [`StateTrigger`] or a custom trigger wins over an [`AdaptiveTrigger`]; among adaptive triggers the larger `MinWindowWidth` wins, then the larger `MinWindowHeight`; then the first in the order of the source.
