Each animation animates the property its `Storyboard.TargetProperty` names on the object its `Storyboard.TargetName` names (both attached properties, inherited from the storyboards around it), or on the object [`set_target`](Self::set_target) gave it. Names are looked up when the storyboard begins: in the elements of the template, or the name scope of the document, of the element given to [`set_target_scope`](Self::set_target_scope); the storyboard of a visual state looks them up where the setters of the state do. [`begin`](Self::begin) starts it on the global clock (without a global clock, its time stays at zero until [`seek`](Self::seek) moves it); [`stop`](Self::stop) removes its values.

classes.name: SwipeControl
classes.doc: A container that reveals commands when its content is swiped (WinUI's `SwipeControl`). [`left_items`](Self::left_items) and [`right_items`](Self::right_items) open with a horizontal swipe, [`top_items`](Self::top_items) and [`bottom_items`](Self::bottom_items) with a vertical one (a control has items of one direction). [`SwipeMode::Reveal`] items stay open for the user to invoke one; [`SwipeMode::Execute`] items invoke their single item when the swipe passes the threshold. One swipe control is open at a time; [`close`](Self::close) closes it. The interaction is WinUI's: an `InteractionTracker` with a `VisualInteractionSource` (on the nearest `ListBoxItem` within five parents, else the control), redirected for touch and pen (decision D7: no mouse drag), with the resting values of WinUI's `ConfigurePositionInertiaRestingValues`; the content follows the tracker through an expression animation of its `Translation`, on the compositor. The template parts are `RootGrid`, `SwipeContentRoot`, `SwipeContentStackPanel`, `ContentRoot` and `InputEater`; each item is a `CommandBarButton` with the theme's `SwipeItemStyle`.

classes.name: SwipeItems

Execute items have one item at most: [`try_add`](Self::try_add) and [`try_set_mode`](Self::try_set_mode) refuse a change that breaks it (WinUI throws); [`add`](Self::add) logs and ignores such an item. Items added to [`items`](Self::items) directly (as markup does) are not checked; a swipe control uses the first item of execute items.

classes.name: SymbolIcon

The template of the theme draws the glyph of [`symbol`](Self::symbol) ([`Symbol::glyph`]) in its text part `PART_Text`, with the font of the theme resource `SymbolThemeFontFamily` (Segoe Fluent Icons in the WinUI theme), 20 pixels, normal style and weight; the foreground is the icon's. The font is not bundled: off Windows an application supplies a symbol font with the same code points and sets `SymbolThemeFontFamily` to it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.2). The WinUI theme has the template; the Fluent and Simple themes have none. Deviation (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, SymbolIcon): WinUI builds the text block in code (`CSymbolIcon::ApplyTemplate`) with the font `Segoe Fluent Icons` written in; here the template is the theme's and the font its resource.

classes.doc: The shadow of the theme (WinUI `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.ThemeShadow`): set as the `Shadow` of an element, the element casts the shadow of its elevation, the Z of its `Translation`, as the controls of WinUI do under their popups (32 for a flyout, 16 for a tool tip, 128 for a content dialog). WinUI 3 draws every theme shadow as a drop shadow ([`is_drop_shadow_mode`](Self::is_drop_shadow_mode)): an ambient and a directional shadow around the element, the darker in the dark theme, none in a high contrast theme. A `ThemeShadow` can be shared by several elements; it has no appearance of its own. [`receivers`](Self::receivers) are the elements the projected shadows of WinUI (the root and the open popups by default) would fall on. WinUI 3 keeps the collection and its validation but does not draw projected shadows, so the receivers do not change the drawing here either.

classes.name: TitleBar
classes.doc: The title bar of a window (WinUI's `TitleBar`): a back button, a pane toggle button, a left header, an icon, a title and a subtitle, content (a search box, in WinUI Gallery) and a right header, drawn in the title bar of the window when the client area extends into it. The control sets the states of WinUI as pseudo-classes, which the control theme of the WinUI theme (`src/FerroUI.Themes.WinUI/Controls/TitleBar.xaml`) styles: `:back-button-visible`, `:pane-toggle-button-visible`, `:left-header-visible`, `:icon-visible`, `:title-text-visible`, `:subtitle-text-visible`, `:content-visible`, `:right-header-visible` (the Visible states of their groups; their absence is Collapsed), `:deactivated` (the Deactivated states: the window is not active), `:expanded-height` (HeightGroup: content or a header), `:compact` (DisplayModeGroup: the content no longer fits beside the title) and `:negative-inset-spacing` (LeftHeaderSpacingGroup). The template parts are WinUI's: `LeftPaddingColumn` and `RightPaddingColumn` (borders in FerroUI, a column definition has no name), `PART_BackButton`, `PART_PaneToggleButton`, `PART_Icon`, `PART_LeftHeaderPresenter`, `PART_ContentPresenterGrid`, `PART_ContentPresenter` and `PART_RightHeaderPresenter`. The Fluent and Simple themes have no template for it (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, section 5.1). The window: WinUI's `AppWindow` gives the insets of the caption buttons, the drag regions and the activation. The port takes the insets from [`Window::caption_button_insets`] (the traffic lights of macOS at the left, the caption buttons the toolkit draws at the right), marks the title bar as the drag region of the window and its back button, pane toggle button, headers and the interactive controls of its content as elements that take the input ([`WindowDecorationProperties`] roles, which take effect while the client area extends into the decorations), and follows [`WindowBase::is_active`]. A title is the title of the window while the bar shows it, as in WinUI.

classes.name: VisualState
classes.doc: A visual state: the values its [`setters`](Self::setters) set while it is the current state of its [`VisualStateGroup`](super::VisualStateGroup). The [`storyboard`](Self::storyboard) of the state runs while it is the current state; the storyboard of the state it leaves stops (its values are removed). The setters are setters with a [`target`](ferroui_base::styling::Setter::target): markup writes `<Setter Target="Element.Property" Value="..."/>`. They are applied at animation priority, above local values and styles, and removed when the group leaves the state (docs/porting/winui-calculator-gaps.md, section 5.5). Deviation (docs/porting/winui-controls.md, VisualStateManager): `x:Name` names the state but does not register it in the name scope, so `find_name` does not find it.

classes.name: VisualStateGroup
classes.doc: A group of mutually exclusive [`VisualState`]s: at most one of them is the [`current_state`](Self::current_state) of the group, null at first. The groups of an element are the attached [`VisualStateManager::visual_state_groups_property`](super::VisualStateManager::visual_state_groups_property); `VisualStateManager::go_to_state` changes the state of the group that has the state of the name it is given.

classes.name: VisualStateManager
classes.doc: Manages the visual states of controls and the transitions between them. The visual states of an element are the [`visual_state_groups_property`](Self::visual_state_groups_property) attached to the root of its visual states: for a templated control the root of its template, for a user control (or any content control, or content page) whose template has none, the control that is its content. [`go_to_state`](Self::go_to_state) makes a state the current state of its group. A custom manager derives from this class, overrides [`go_to_state_core`](VisualStateManagerImpl::go_to_state_core) and is set on the root with [`set_custom_visual_state_manager`](Self::set_custom_visual_state_manager).

classes.name: VisualTransition
classes.doc: How a [`VisualStateGroup`](super::VisualStateGroup) changes from one state to another when `GoToState` is called with transitions (WinUI's `VisualTransition`). A transition applies from the state named [`from`](Self::from) (empty: any) to the state named [`to`](Self::to) (empty: any). It runs its [`storyboard`](Self::storyboard) and, over [`generated_duration`](Self::generated_duration) eased by [`generated_easing_function`](Self::generated_easing_function), animations it generates from the values of the old state to those of the new one; the setters and the storyboard of the new state apply when they have completed.

classes.name: XamlCompositionBrushBase
classes.doc: A brush that paints an area with a composition brush (WinUI `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.XamlCompositionBrushBase`). A subclass creates its [`composition_brush`](Self::composition_brush) when the brush is first used in a window that has a compositor (`OnConnected`) and releases it when no element of such a window uses it any more (`OnDisconnected`). The compositor paints the composition brush inside the shape the brush fills, as the brushes of WinUI's composition are painted; where no composition brush is set, and where the brush is drawn without a compositor (an image of a visual drawn by the immediate renderer), the area is filled with [`fallback_color`](Self::fallback_color).

classes.name: XamlLight
classes.doc: A light of the object model (WinUI `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.XamlLight`). A subclass gives the light an id ([`get_id`](XamlLightImpl::get_id)) and creates its composition light when the light is connected to the element that holds it ([`on_connected`](XamlLightImpl::on_connected)), setting it with [`set_composition_light`](Self::set_composition_light). The light then lights, in the subtree of that element: - the elements that target its id ([`add_target_element`](Self::add_target_element)): their composition visuals are targets of the composition light, which lights their content; - the XAML brushes that target its id ([`add_target_brush`](Self::add_target_brush)): the scene lighting effects of those brushes receive the light. The composition light is in the coordinates of the element that holds it (its `CoordinateSpace` is the composition visual of that element).
